newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dollar/Swiss gains keep dollar buoyant.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dollar/Swiss gains keep dollar buoyant.

text.p: The dollar looks poised to continue its current march higher against the Swiss franc, pulling dollar/mark along with it, technical analysts said.
The greenback on Wednesday broke through the tops of triangle patterns against the Swiss and mark and should be able to extend those gains in the near term, chartists said.

"Dollar/Swiss looks very good. Momentum is maintained to the upside as long as we stay above 1.3280," said Thom Worden, vice president in the global technical analysis group at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Dollar/Swiss later pulled back from resistance at 1.3410 and also faces a 19-month bull channel resistance at 1.3480, chartists said.

The recent gains in dollar/Swiss, as well as the continued health of mark/Swiss, are keeping dollar/mark bid as well, technicians noted. But dollar/mark looks a bit less bullish, with near-term resistance at 1.5580 and 1.5640 before the 1996 high at 1.5735.
"Dollar/mark broke a falling resistance line at 1.5580, but it's not out of the longer-term range," said Scott Siller, technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch.
"There's no clear sign of an upside break yet," in dollar/mark, Siller added.
Also restraining dollar/mark is the apparent cap in sterling/mark near 2.60, chartists said. A close below 2.59 could yield eventual losses to 2.57 and 2.55.
"We've seen a completion of a corrective upwave, and we could still have another corresponding spike lower," said Worden.
Dollar/yen is also struggling to escape a triangle, with a rising support line gradually shaking out bears, analysts said. Current support sits at 113.40, with a cap at 114.30.
"The bulls are maintaining the highs, but the bears are losing footing, so there's an upward bias," Siller said.
The double-top at 114.80 and 114.92 yen remains a formidable obstacle, with another four big figures seen on the upside if it falls, chartists said.

Mark/yen has held doggedly to support at 73.05/10, but analysts continue to call for an imminent slump. Bearish daily studies suggest a break to 72.70 and 72.55, with current resistance at 73.40 and 73.80.
It looks vulnerable. It looks like it's going to signal lower," Siller said. ((--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664))
